objective: Compose existing source-tested TCS1-4 selectors with scheduled DCS2 gift materialization and the established event lifecycle, using explicitly supplied root-water and daily stress observations.
dependency_review: The current scheduled process supports only TCS7/8 and directly performs timing followed by common depth/rate/event materialization. Approximately 80 runner/tool references compile mod_irrigation_process; importing the standalone TCS1-4 module into that core would introduce broad compile-order churn. Prefer an explicit process composition entry with a factored common post-timing path, plus a separate bridge depending on both modules. Do not fabricate hydraulic sensor values or thresholds to force TCS7 to impersonate another selector.
design_constraints: Retain the existing ordinary scheduled entry and TCS7/8 behavior unchanged.
Share eligibility, pending-event continuation, DCS2 amount/rate and event materialization rather than duplicate those equations.
The bridge must call evaluate_tcs1_4_timing; preserve strict comparison and existing source AFGEN arithmetic.
Externally supplied observations are explicit immutable inputs, not claimed to be internally derived crop/root or daily accumulator state.
Do not consult a new selector for a pending gift or consume selection opportunity on rejected trials.
Keep initial composition process-only; extend source/runtime/application binding only after executable process gates pass.
first_gates: All four selectors trigger and decline at source-defined strict boundaries.
False timing leaves no selected gift; true timing reuses DCS2 depth, source rate and duration.
Existing eligibility and fixed-event precedence remain effective.
Pending continuation, split-required and retry preserve input state.
Malformed selector observations/tables fail closed on selection; TCS7/8 preservation and source oracle remain passing at O0/O2.
non_goals: No automatic daily stress accumulator, root-water derivation, calendar/parser, solute transport, general registry or canonical admission. Existing initial zero-source numerical issue is independent and remains open.
next: Factor the scheduled post-timing path without changing its legacy entry, implement the typed selector bridge and bounded independent process tests, then qualify before runtime integration.
